title: Pullback of a homogeneous fraction relation between projective charts
statement: Let $A=\bigoplus_{i\geq0}A_i$ be a nonnegatively graded commutative ring, $X$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $d>0$, $s\in A_d$, and $U\subseteq X$ an open subscheme. Write $A_{(s)}$ for the degree-zero homogeneous localization and $D_+(s)\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_{(s)}$ for the projective chart [def-pc-proj]. Let $\rho:A_{(s)}\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ring map and $q:U\to\operatorname{Spec}A_{(s)}$ a morphism whose map on global sections agrees with $\rho$ under the canonical Spec and restriction identifications [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]. Put $g=\iota_s\circ q$. Let $e,n,N\geq0$, $t\in A_e$, $\xi\in A_{ne}$, and $p,r\in A_{Nd}$, with $\xi p=rt^n$ in $A$. Put $W=\operatorname{image}_X(g^{-1}D_+(t))$. Then in $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_X)$ one has $g^\sharp(\xi/t^n)\,\rho(p/s^N)|_W=\rho(r/s^N)|_W$. Here $\xi/t^n$ denotes the canonical degree-zero fraction section on $D_+(t)$, also when $e=0$.

proof.text: Pass both chart fractions to the homogeneous localization at ts. The maps send xi/t^n to xi*s^n/(ts)^n, and p/s^N and r/s^N to p*t^N/(ts)^N and r*t^N/(ts)^N. Cross multiplication, with localization witness 1, reduces their product equality to xi*p=r*t^n multiplied by s^n*t^N*(ts)^N. Lean uses awayMap_mk, Away.val_mk, val_injective, Localization.mk_mul, mk_eq_mk_iff and r_iff_exists, followed by ring. No denominator cancellation occurs.

The inverse s-chart map pulls D_+(s) back to the whole affine chart, so g inverse image of D_+(t) lies over D_+(ts). Pull back the canonical map from the localization at ts to its projective basic-open sections. Proj.awayMap_awayToSection and Scheme.Hom.map_appLE identify the two localization maps with the original chart-section pullbacks.

Use basicOpenToSpec_app_top and the inverse chart isomorphism to show that the s-chart pullback on global sections is GammaSpecIso.inv. Composition with q and hq identifies this with rho followed by U.topIso.inv. Restrict and use topIso to obtain the ambient restriction on W. Apply this ring map to the fraction product equality. It preserves multiplication, giving the conclusion. The private Lean helpers inclusion_top and away_top prove the restriction and inverse-chart identifications.
